rules.statement: Keep presentational React components stateless: they must not read the Redux store, dispatch, or hold fetch/server state, and may keep local state only when it is intrinsic to a control and still renders in isolation.
rules.why: Presentational components must render in Storybook and under React Testing Library without a store; state in them breaks that isolation, and the ADR makes breaking the layering a review failure.
rules.check: Look for useSelector/useDispatch, typed store hooks, RTK Query hooks, fetch calls or data-loading useEffect inside components in the design-system package or presentational component files.

rules.statement: Wire Redux and RTK Query only in containers at the top of a screen, and move non-trivial logic out of components into UI-free modules with their own unit tests.
rules.why: Logic in components breaks unit isolation; the layering keeps each layer testable on its own.
rules.check: Look for non-trivial computation, parsing or decision logic in component bodies with no UI-free module and unit test, and for store wiring placed below the screen-level container.

rules.statement: Use RTK Query for server state by default, not hand-rolled fetch-plus-slice or component-local fetching.
rules.why: Redux Toolkit with RTK Query gives one state model for server and client state, matching the stateless and stateful layering.
rules.check: Look for new manual fetch/axios calls that store server data in useState or custom slices where an RTK Query endpoint would do.

rules.statement: Import a shared workspace package only through its public entry point, never through a deep path into its source.
rules.why: Each shared package is used only through its public entry point so that its internals can change without breaking consumers.
rules.check: Look for imports like '@scope/pkg/src/...' or relative paths reaching into another package's folder.

rules.statement: Keep the design-system package free of any store dependency and the store, config and API-contract packages free of UI (and the API-contract package free of Redux); put a stateful container used by more than one app in the shared shell package, and keep one used by a single app in that app.
rules.why: A store-backed container in the UI package breaks its stateless, store-free contract, and one in the store package makes the UI-free state package depend on Material UI; the shell package is the one place allowed to depend on both.
rules.check: Check new package.json dependencies and imports: store/Redux imports in the UI package, MUI/React UI imports in store/config/api packages, and shared containers duplicated across apps or single-app containers placed in a shared package.

rules.statement: Don't bake tier- or environment-specific values into a frontend bundle at build time; read them at runtime from the configuration document the serving host publishes (or from the host-rendered page).
rules.why: A bundle is built once and must run unchanged in every tier; per-environment bundles invite a mismatch between bundle and configuration.
rules.check: Look for environment-specific URLs, client ids, issuers or feature flags in import.meta.env, Vite define, .env.* files or hard-coded constants.

rules.statement: Type a name set that new consumers may extend (such as surface or app names) as the known literals plus `(string & {})` rather than a closed union.
rules.why: Vocabularies are open unless provably closed; a closed union forces every new consumer to edit a library, while an unknown name falls back to a default and fails visibly.
rules.check: Look for new closed string-literal unions in shared packages for values a new app or host could add.

rules.statement: Have a component that loads data at boot take its loader as a prop (e.g. a `(signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>` function) instead of importing and calling a loader module itself.
rules.why: A test can then pass its own loader instead of mocking a module, and a surface that loads differently can reuse the component.
rules.check: Look for gate or boot components that import a loader directly or choose their load from a string prop, and tests that use vi.mock to control such loading.

rules.statement: Keep each app's `main.tsx` as the explicit composition root that creates the root, the store Provider and the boot gate, and bind app-specific identity (such as the surface name) only there; don't hide this in a mount helper or per-app bootstrap module.
rules.why: Hiding the Provider hides the requirement that the gate sits inside it, and per-app bootstrap copies differ by one string and drift.
rules.check: Look for helpers that wrap createRoot/Provider, new per-app bootstrap.ts files, or app modules other than main.tsx binding the origin or surface name.

rules.statement: Default a runtime-configuration request's origin to `location.origin` instead of hard-coding or passing a host origin from app code.
rules.why: The serving host is the origin of every bundle, because a standalone dev server proxies the bootstrap document.
rules.check: Look for absolute origins or base URLs passed to the configuration loader in app code.

rules.statement: In a management UI, model platform, team and tenant scopes as distinct browsing contexts with their own navigation, cache tags and authorization gating, never as one list filtered by scope.
rules.why: The management surface has to show the security boundary between platform, team and tenant.
rules.check: Look for screens or queries that merge resources across scopes into one filtered list, or share cache tags or authorization checks across scopes.

rules.statement: Get theme tokens and branding through the design system's theme provider, not through hard-coded colors or branding in components.
rules.why: Branding arrives at runtime from the bootstrap document or the host-rendered page, so it has to flow through the provider.
rules.check: Look for hard-coded colors, logos or brand strings in components instead of theme lookups.

rules.statement: Give each new stateless design-system component, including loading and error views, Storybook stories.
rules.why: Presentational components are meant to render in Storybook without a store; the boot loading and error views ship with stories.
rules.check: Look for new components in the design-system package that have no matching *.stories.tsx file.
